claims.claim: Modern heat pumps deliver three to four units of heat for every unit of electricity they consume (coefficient of performance of 3-4).
claims.episode_span: routinely achieve coefficients of performance between three and four, meaning they deliver three to four units of heat for every unit of electricity supplied
claims.source_title: Electric heat pumps use much less energy than furnaces, and can cool houses too - The Conversation
claims.supporting_quote: Modern heat pump systems can transfer three or four times more thermal energy in the form of heat than they consume in electrical energy to do this work

claims.claim: A conventional furnace's efficiency is capped at 100%, while a heat pump used for building heating can exceed 100% because it moves heat rather than generating it.
claims.episode_span: Burning fuel for heat hits a hard 100% efficiency wall, yet heat pumps routinely deliver three to four times more heat than the electricity they consume by moving heat instead of creating it.
claims.supporting_quote: the theoretical limit for a conventional furnace's instantaneous efficiency is 100%, whereas a heat pump used for building heating may exceed 100%. For example, a COP of 1.5 is equivalent to 150%.

claims.claim: Heat pumps do not create heat; they absorb existing heat from outside and transfer it indoors.
claims.episode_span: most of that heat already exists in the outside air or ground, and the real expense is only the modest work required to concentrate and move it indoors
claims.supporting_quote: This is because heat pumps don't actually create heat, they just transfer it from one place to another. The system absorbs existing heat through refrigerant lines and releases that heat into your home

claims.claim: A gas furnace is typically the lower-cost installation (several thousand dollars), while a comparable heat-pump installation often costs more upfront.
claims.episode_span: The finished cost of a typical residential gas furnace plus ductwork runs on the order of several thousand dollars, while a comparable heat-pump installation often lands higher
claims.source_title: How Much Does It Cost to Install a Heat Pump vs. Furnace? | Filterbuy
claims.supporting_quote: A high-efficiency gas furnace (96% AFUE) remains the lower-cost install at $3,500–$10,000+, but factor in that it requires a separate AC unit, a heat pump at $3,800–$25,000+ covers both heating and cooling in one system.

claims.claim: Cold-climate heat pump performance has been addressed by variable-speed, inverter-driven compressors.
claims.episode_span: Cold-climate performance concerns, although largely addressed by variable-speed compressors and improved refrigerants in the last decade
claims.source_title: Can Heat Pumps Actually Work in Cold Climates? - Consumer Reports
claims.supporting_quote: The key feature in a cold-climate heat pump is a variable-speed compressor, powered by an inverter.
